annotations.title: Apply a character style to a range

description: Apply an existing character style (Zeichenformat) to the characters start_index (inclusive) to end_index (exclusive) of the story of a text frame. The style must exist (define_character_style; list_paragraph_styles lists them). Never changes text. Returns frame_id, characters_affected, style_applied and tracking {effective, character_style, paragraph_style}: a character style that carries its own tracking replaces the tracking of the paragraph style for that range (it is not added) – a paragraph style with tracking 100 plus a character style with tracking 260 gives 260, visibly wider. effective is what InDesign uses at the first character of the range; character_style is null when the style leaves tracking alone. Stories managed by an editorial workflow (InCopy) that are not checked out here (lock_state checked_in_story, locked_story, missing_lock_state or mixed_lock_state) are refused before anything is written: invalid_state with details.code "story_locked" (details: frame_id, story_id, lock_state, managed_file) – check the story out in the editorial system or in InCopy first.

document_id.description: Document to act on, from list_documents or open_document. Without it the frontmost document is used. A document opened with show_window false is never the active one and must always be addressed by id.

end_index.description: End of the range (exclusive); must be greater than start_index.

start_index.description: First character of the range (inclusive), a story index from get_frame_text.
